topics.name: Polite requests and offers (could, may, would, shall)
Talking about the future (will, going to, present continuous)

options: May I borrows your pen, please?
May I borrow your pen, please?
May I borrowed your pen, please?
questions.rule: After may, use the base form of the verb: May I borrow ...?

options: Parents is invited to the function.
Parents are invite to the function.
Parents are invited to the function.
questions.rule: Passive = be + past participle. Plural parents takes are invited.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: inaugurate
inaugurated
inaugurating

questions.rule: Going to is followed by the base form of the verb: going to inaugurate.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: aren't
don't
won't

questions.rule: The tag repeats the helping verb: You are ... → aren't you?

questions.after: you please open the hall door?
options: Shall
Are
Could
questions.rule: Could you please + base verb ...? is a polite request. Shall you and Are you open are wrong here.

questions.after: start at ten in the morning.
options: is
will
are
questions.rule: Will + base verb talks about the future: will start.
A polite request for permission: May I + base verb ...?

chat: What are you going to do on Sunday?
options: I going to attend a function at school.
I am go to attend a function at school.
I am going to attend a function at school.
questions.rule: Future plan: am/is/are + going to + base verb = I am going to attend.

chat: The function starts at ten, doesn't it?
options: Yes, it do. Don't be late.
Yes, it does. Don't be late.
Yes, it done. Don't be late.
questions.rule: A short answer repeats the helping verb of the tag: doesn't it? → Yes, it does.

options: Copies was made by the students.
Copies were made by the students.
Copies were make by the students.
questions.rule: Simple past passive: was/were + past participle. Plural copies takes were made.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: Ms Naik will inaugurate the project, doesn't she?
Ms Naik will inaugurate the project, isn't she?
Ms Naik will inaugurate the project, won't she?
questions.rule: Will in the statement → won't in the tag.

options: Sameer told that he was busy with the project.
Sameer said me that he was busy with the project.
Sameer told me that he was busy with the project.
questions.rule: Told needs a person after it (told me); said does not (said that).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: were
is
be

questions.rule: Plural invitations + past time takes were: were sent.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: visited
visit
visits

questions.rule: Going to is followed by the base form: going to visit.

questions.after: I help you with the chairs, ma'am?
options: Shall
Does
Am
questions.rule: To offer help, use Shall I ...? with the base verb.

questions.before: Sameer told his mother that the function
options: was
were
are
questions.rule: After past told, the reported verb moves back: was. Function is singular.
Passive: was + past participle + by + doer (by her).

chat: You are going to take part in the project, aren't you?
options: Yes, I am, Mummy.
Yes, I do, Mummy.
Yes, I are, Mummy.
questions.rule: The question uses are you, so the short answer with I is Yes, I am.

options: The project is important, isn't it?
The project is important, is it?
The project is important, doesn't it?
questions.rule: Positive statement with is → negative tag isn't it?

options: Sameer said that I was happy.
Sameer said that he was happy.
Sameer said that he were happy.
questions.rule: I → he (Sameer), and am → was after past said.

options: This Sunday is going to be a busy day.
This Sunday are going to be a busy day.
This Sunday is going be a busy day.
questions.rule: Sunday is singular: is going to + base verb = is going to be.

options: The notice were put up on the board yesterday.
The notice is put up on the board yesterday.
The notice was put up on the board yesterday.
questions.rule: Yesterday needs the past passive; singular notice takes was put up.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: don't
didn't
wasn't

questions.rule: The verb sent is simple past, so the tag uses did: didn't they?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: tell
telling
tells

questions.rule: A reported request uses asked + person + to + base verb: asked the students to tell.

questions.after: like your paper to cover the function.
options: are
have
would
questions.rule: Would like is the polite way to say want.

questions.after: inaugurated by Ms Naik last Sunday.
options: is
was
were
questions.rule: Last Sunday is past and project is singular: was inaugurated.
Polite request: Could you please + base verb ...?

chat: What did your teacher say about Sunday?
options: She said that the function will started at ten.
She said me that the function would start at ten.
She said that the function would start at ten.
questions.rule: After past said, will becomes would + base verb. Never said me.

options: No, I visiting my grandparents in Pune.
No, I am visiting my grandparents in Pune.
No, I am visit my grandparents in Pune.
questions.rule: A fixed future plan can use the present continuous: I am visiting.

options: The invitation was prepared by the Principal.
The invitation is prepared by the Principal.
The invitation was prepare by the Principal.
questions.rule: Prepared is simple past, so the passive is was + past participle: was prepared.

options: Daddy and I can't both go, but one of us will comes with you.
Daddy and I can't both goes, but one of us will come with you.
Daddy and I can't both go, but one of us will come with you.
questions.rule: After can't and will, always use the base form: go, come.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: You have sent the invitation, haven't you?
You have sent the invitation, didn't you?
You have sent the invitation, hasn't you?
questions.rule: Present perfect have sent → tag with have: haven't you?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: lent
lend
lends

questions.rule: After can, use the base form of the verb: Can you please lend ...?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: are
was
be

questions.rule: Two plural subjects joined by and take a plural verb: are invited.

questions.before: Ms Naik is the President of Sahayak Samaj,
options: doesn't
isn't
wasn't
questions.rule: Statement with is → tag isn't she? (same tense, same helping verb).

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a question tag.
questions.rule: Positive statement with will → negative tag won't you?
Reported speech: said that + would (for will) + base verb.

questions.prompt: Pick the correct reply on the phone.
options: Good morning. Could I speaking to the editor, please?
Good morning. Could I spoke to the editor, please?
Good morning. Could I speak to the editor, please?
questions.rule: Could I + base verb is a polite phone request: Could I speak to ...?

questions.source: Ms Naik will inaugurate the project.
options: Will Ms Naik inaugurates the project?
Does Ms Naik will inaugurate the project?
Will Ms Naik inaugurate the project?
questions.rule: Put will before the subject and keep the base verb: Will Ms Naik inaugurate ...?

options: The parents were invited by the teachers.
The parents are invite by the teachers.
The parents are invited by the teachers.
questions.rule: Simple present passive: am/is/are + past participle = are invited.

options: The editor said that he had made a note of the date.
The editor said that he had make a note of the date.
The editor said me that he had made a note of the date.
questions.rule: Have made becomes had made after past said; said takes no person after it.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: There is a function on Sunday, isn't it?
There is a function on Sunday, is there?
There is a function on Sunday, isn't there?
questions.rule: A sentence starting There is keeps there in the tag: isn't there?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: inaugurated
inaugurating
inaugurates

questions.rule: Every passive needs be + past participle: to be inaugurated.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: spoke
told
talked

questions.rule: Use told when the listener follows (told the students that); said takes no listener.

options: to arrange
arranging
arrange
questions.rule: Would you mind is followed by the -ing form: mind arranging.
Future passive: will be + past participle; the phrasal verb keeps over: presided over by.

chat: What did Mr Ajinkya ask you to do?
options: He asked us to tell our parents about the project.
He asked us that tell our parents about the project.
He asked to us tell our parents about the project.
questions.rule: Reported request: asked + person + to + base verb = asked us to tell.

chat: What are your plans for the summer holidays?
options: We going to visit Goa, and I will learn swimming there.
We are going to visit Goa, and I will learning swimming there.
We are going to visit Goa, and I will learn swimming there.
questions.rule: Are going to + base verb and will + base verb: visit, learn.

questions.source: Mummy said to me, "I will come with you."
options: Mummy told me that I would come with her.
Mummy told me that she would come with me.
Mummy told me that she would came with me.
questions.rule: I → she, you → me, will come → would come.

questions.source: The invitations were sent by the student secretaries.
options: The student secretaries were sent the invitations.
The student secretaries sent the invitations.
The student secretaries send the invitations.
questions.rule: The doer after by becomes the subject; keep the simple past: sent.
